title: fix(plugin-gantt): key the record fetch on values, not on memo identities
body:
Fixes #10036

Clause-②: no — an internal hook dependency array. It moves no exported symbol and no key on a published payload.

The ninth and tenth instances of the class ruled on objectui#8640 (`AGENTS.md` §5 commandment **#10**), both sitting on one seam in `packages/plugin-gantt/src/ObjectGantt.tsx`. ⛔ The direction is not re-argued here; the commandment already decided it.

## Premise, re-taken on `origin/main` before any edit

All three legs held, the card's own control included:

1. `reload`'s dependency array listed `effectiveDataSource`, and `effectiveDataSource` is a `useMemo` result.
2. The mount effect listed `reload`, a `useCallback` result.
3. ⭐ The file's first-person record is still there: `dataItems` was removed from that same array because a discard «was enough to give `reload` a fresh identity and re-fire the mount effect below (objectui#6592)». One banned identity came off that line and another was left on it — finding the removal **and** the survivor in the same read is what says the instrument was reading rather than guessing.

## Why this is not theoretical on this component

`resolveDataSource` (`@object-ui/core`) answers `provider: 'object'` with the context adapter **unchanged**, but **constructs** a new `ApiDataSource` for `'api'` and a new `ValueDataSource` for `'value'`. So on those two providers a discarded memo hands back a fresh adapter for a byte-identical authored config, rebuilds `reload`, and re-fires the mount effect — one redundant round trip, per discard, on a view nobody touched.

`ObjectGantt.discardedConfigMemo.test.tsx` already named exactly this gap in its own docblock as a "Known boundary" for the `api` / `value` providers. This PR measures it.

⚠️ **Fixing leg 1 alone would have been unobservable and would not have closed the defect.** A discarded `useCallback` yields a fresh function whatever its own dependency list says — an empty list included — so the mount effect would still have re-fired. Both sides of the seam, or neither holds.

## The repair

- `effectiveDataSourceRef` — `reload` **reads** the adapter through a ref refreshed on every render, so it is always the adapter the current render resolved, and never a reason to rebuild the callback.
- `adapterInputsKey` — `reload` and the fetch effect **key** on what `resolveDataSource` actually reads out of the authored config, per provider arm (`read` + `write` for `api`, `items` for `value`, nothing but the fallback otherwise), alongside the host's `dataSource` and `apiFetch`. Those three are that memo's own dependency list, with the memoised `dataConfig` replaced by the values it is derived from.
- `reloadRef` — the fetch effect calls through a ref and repeats the same value list instead of naming `reload`.

⛔ No lint rule was silenced and no `eslint-disable` was added. The one disable on `reload`'s array is pre-existing and still says what it said (`(rest as any).data` intentionally untracked). `pnpm exec eslint` on both changed files exits **0** with no errors; the count of react-hooks findings in `ObjectGantt.tsx` went **down** by one against the pre-fix file, measured by linting the pre-fix content beside it in one `--format json` run. Two new `react-hooks/refs` warnings appear for the two render-phase ref writes — the rule this repo deliberately downgraded to `warn`, and the same idiom `app-shell`'s `AdapterProvider` and `MetadataProvider` already use for a `useMemo` result.

### ⛔ Why the key is the per-arm slice and not the whole config

The first attempt keyed on the whole config's deep value, and the objectui#6592 pin caught it: that pin moves an inert field inside `schema.data` which "is read by nothing under test", and the fetch must not re-fire. The whole-config key made that authored-but-inert byte a refetch trigger on the `object` provider — where the adapter is the context DataSource and the config contributes nothing to it at all. That is a **widening**, so it was withdrawn. The note above `dataItems` says such an input "cannot be flattened to a fixed primitive list"; true of a fixed **list**, and the reason it gives is right — the `api` arm's input is a whole request config. A per-arm **value** is expressible, and it is the one that neither widens nor narrows.

## The forced-discard pin: achievable, and it discriminates

**Yes.** `packages/plugin-gantt/src/ObjectGantt.discardedReloadIdentity-10036.test.tsx` follows `packages/permissions/src/__tests__/providerCtxIdentity.discarded.test.tsx`: it patches `useMemo` **and** `useCallback` at the module level through `vi.mock('react', …)` — the only patch the component's own `import` bindings see — and fires a discard on demand by bumping an epoch appended to every armed dependency list. It arms **every** memo and callback in the tree rather than matching a marker, because a marker on `effectiveDataSource` alone would leave `reload`'s own `useCallback` un-discarded, which is the half leg 2 names.

The observable is a **request count**, not an identity compare: requests are served by a double passed as `apiFetch`, so nothing reaches happy-dom's origin and is attributed to this file by the network-escape guard. The proxy carries its own self-check (`provesTheProxyDiscriminates`), and an "armed but not fired" re-render inside the pin proves a green cannot come from the proxy having broken caching outright.

### RED before, GREEN after — file state proved in the same command as each run

The ablation restores the **pre-fix** `ObjectGantt.tsx` from the branch point while the pin file stays byte-identical, proves the swap by object hash, runs, restores from `HEAD`, proves the restore by hash **and** by an empty `git status --porcelain`, and runs again. ⛔ No leg concludes anything from an exit code.

```
HEAD blob (fixed)   : c66fbe8111154b0bbe4f63e3cd9df02b53f9ebbc
BASE blob (pre-fix) : 597ed278784343c95241c38452d1d57260ce761d

######## LEG 1 — MUTATION (pre-fix source, pin unchanged) ########
on-disk blob now    : 597ed278784343c95241c38452d1d57260ce761d
marker 'adapterInputsKey' occurrences: 0   (expect 0 on the pre-fix file)
marker 'effectiveDataSourceRef' occurrences: 0   (expect 0 on the pre-fix file)
pin blob            : 1e9d2b1870a54544e446918aff04fa88e610dcf6   (unchanged across both legs)
--- run ---
  [
    "A /api/gantt/tasks",
+   "A /api/gantt/tasks",
+   "A /api/gantt/tasks",
  ]
 Test Files  1 failed (1)
      Tests  1 failed | 5 passed (6)
LEG1 vitest exit: 1

######## LEG 2 — RESTORE (the committed fix) ########
on-disk blob now    : c66fbe8111154b0bbe4f63e3cd9df02b53f9ebbc
git status --porcelain after restore: ''   (expect empty)
marker 'adapterInputsKey' occurrences: 5   (expect > 0)
--- run ---
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  6 passed (6)
LEG2 vitest exit: 0
```

Two readings the numbers carry beyond "it went red":

- The defect issues **one extra request per discard** — two discards, three requests — which is the mechanism, not a one-off.
- The five non-regression pins pass on the **pre-fix** source too. That is what a non-regression axis must do: they fail on the plausible wrong fix (dropping the dependency and refetching for nothing), not on the bug.

### What the non-regression pins hold

A changed `api` endpoint, a changed authored `filter`, a swapped `apiFetch`, and a swapped context adapter each still refetch, and the **new** double is the one that runs in the last two. `resource`, `dataProvider` and `hasInlineData` are derived from the authored config the first pins move; `objectSchema` and `perms` are unchanged members of the same list.

## Gates, re-run as the last action before the push

At commit `19d1eebf1`, tree equal to the pushed commit, `git status --porcelain` empty, each run printing that state in the same command. All files **tracked** at the time of the run, so the populations include this change rather than collapsing around it — the scanned counts moved with it (8120 text files, 5188 source files, 3341 test files).

| gate | exit |
|---|---|
| `check-changeset-presence` | 0 — 2 source files of 1 released package changed, 1 changeset declared |
| `check-changeset-no-major` / `-fixed` / `-overwrite` / `-claims` | 0 |
| `check-control-bytes` | 0 |
| `check-new-cross-file-line-citations` | 0 new citations |
| `check-vi-mock-specifiers` / `-inherit` / `-override-shape` | 0 |
| `check-test-path-roots` | 0 |
| `check-unreferenced-sources` | 0 |
| `check-governed-queue-guard --test` | NOT GOVERNED — 3 paths, none matched |
| `eslint` on both changed files | 0, no errors |
| `type-check` (`tsc --noEmit` + `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`) | 0 |
| `vitest run packages/plugin-gantt/` | 0 — 70 files, 544 tests |

The changeset is a real `patch` on `@object-ui/plugin-gantt`, decided by running the gate, not from memory: the gate names `src/` files of a released package, and a removed redundant round trip is user-visible.

⚠️ The first full-package run **failed** — the objectui#6592 pin, on the too-wide key described above. It is green now; the sequence is recorded because the pin doing its job is the reason the key was narrowed.

## Is a mechanical guard owed? — triage's question, answered

**Yes for this shape, and the sweep's own two finds are the argument.** Commandment #10 records that a lint rule is feasible for the same-file shape only, `eslint-rules/` being where it would live, with the cross-module instances out of reach of any single-file rule. Both instances this sweep produced are **same-file**: `reload` and `effectiveDataSource` are declared in one component here, and objectui#10044's `candidateSignature = useMemo(…, [candidates])` sits directly under the `candidates` memo in `useRecordSearch.ts`. ⇒ The two that a per-class remediation would have had to catch are exactly the two a feasible rule reaches. ⛔ Filing and writing it is outside this card's file surface; it is reported for the seat to file rather than smuggled in here.

## Acceptance notes — noticed, not fixed here

- **A record query fires twice when the context adapter is swapped on `provider: 'object'`.** `useSettledSchema` re-reads `getObjectSchema` through the new adapter and settles a **fresh** definition object for a byte-identical answer; `objectSchema` is a genuine member of the fetch effect's value list, so the record query runs a second time. That is the seam commandment #10 spells out in as many words — "a provider that refetches may not republish an equal payload as a new object" — one link upstream, in `packages/react/src/hooks/useSettledSchema.ts`, outside this card's file surface. It is unchanged by this PR (before and after alike). The new pin deliberately does **not** pin the exact count for that case, so it will not go red on the day it is repaired; it pins that the new adapter is the one that runs. Reported for filing.
- The same file still names `effectiveDataSource` in four **write-back / delete** callback dependency arrays. Those are handler identities: a discard re-creates a handler, it does not issue a request, so no correctness rests on them and they are out of this card's scope. Noted, not filed.
